subject: Streaming & I/O token constraints — post-demo qualification and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Ashraf <samira.ashraf@olivehealth.com>, it-security@olivehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming & I/O token constraints — post-demo recap

Hi Samira — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + what we need to qualify SLOs for the POC: 

Key customer goals we heard:
- Endpoint latency target: 250ms median for interactive clinician flows (95th under 600ms)
- Throughput: 120 requests/min sustained during batch ingestion windows
- Streaming: client-side incremental doc stitching + partial responses for long notes (we discussed chunked streaming)

Open technical questions we need from you to size a canary:
1) Typical input size distribution: median and 95th percentile token counts (input only). If you can attach a few representative payloads (PII-redacted) that helps our profiling.
2) Expected output lengths: are you expecting multi-paragraph summaries (>=1k tokens) or short structured outputs (~100-300 tokens)?
3) Concurrency per user vs total concurrency: Do multiple clinicians call the same patient session concurrently? Approx peak concurrent requests.
4) Streaming behavior: do you require incremental token delivery (server -> client) as model generates, or is client polling acceptable?

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- We'll run local latency/throughput microbenchmarks against a model variant with your sample payloads once you share them.
- Propose a 2-week canary using reserved Dedicated capacity: 2 x A100-equivalent nodes, batching disabled for streaming sessions; autoscale tests for 4x load spikes.
- Provide a draft mutual action plan and performance KPIs (I attached the recording + a small checklist).

Attachments: [olive-demo-recording.mp4 (35MB)], [redwood-latency-benchmarks-4k.pdf (6 pages)]

If possible please drop sample payloads into the shared Drive link below or reply with attachments. Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra/security folks to walk the data flow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samira Ashraf <samira.ashraf@olivehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: it-security@olivehealth.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming & I/O token constraints — post-demo recap

Karthik — great session. Answers inline below and I've attached a sanitized sample payload file.

- Input sizes: median input ~420 tokens (chiefly SOAP notes + metadata). 95th ~2,300 tokens (long consult notes). See attached olive-payload-sample.json (PII masked).
- Output expectations: For summary workflows we expect ~150-300 tokens. For discharge briefings we expect 800-1,200 tokens occasionally.
- Concurrency: typical clinic has ~8 concurrent clinicians; peak clinic-wide concurrency ~60 simultaneous requests during morning shift.
- Streaming: streaming is required for the clinician UI — incremental partial text is critical so the UI shows progress as the model synthesizes long notes.

Security note: our SecOps flagged request/response retention and KV cache persistence; they asked for details on data-at-rest encryption and audit logs. They’re on the CC.

Attached: [olive-payload-sample.json]. I uploaded the larger data sample to your Drive link.

—Samira
Product Lead, Clinical UX | OliveHealth

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming & I/O token constraints — post-demo recap

Marissa / Karthik — quick internal notes after Samira's payloads:

- The 95th input (2.3k tokens) + occasional 1k output means per-request token budget could hit ~3.5k tokens. With streaming required, we should avoid large batching; continuous KV caching still helps for repeated context across the session.
- Latency modeling: to hit 250ms median we need a model with ~optimized decoder path and local KV cache hits. For 95th token ranges (~3.5k total) expect tail latency >1s unless we use a smaller quantized variant or progressive decoding (send partial summaries earlier).
- Canary proposal tweak: start with 3 x A100-equivalent for the dedicated canary, enable progressive-output streaming (flush partial tokens at fixed intervals) and test token-throttling policy to protect p99.
- Ask SecOps for retention window requirement; we need to know whether we must persist request/response for 30/90/365 days — affects storage & audit config.

I'll draft the performance KPIs and a canary runbook. Karthik — can you propose a schedule to sync with OliveHealth SecOps (Samira looped) and ask for the retention SLA?

Ben
Principal SWRE, Performance | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Ashraf <samira.ashraf@olivehealth.com>, it-security@olivehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming & I/O token constraints — post-demo recap

Thanks Samira — got the sample payload JSON and the Drive upload. Next concrete items so we can start profiling and schedule the POC: 

1) SecOps ask: please confirm retention window (choices: 30 / 90 / 365 days). If you prefer not to put a number in email, we can cover this in the SecOps call.
2) Can you share a rough SLA target for p99 latency (helpful for guardrails)? You mentioned 600ms as a rough upper bound in the demo.
3) Data exchange: we've created a secured SFTP token + Drive folder. I added a stub runbook in the Drive with instructions for sample payload upload. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Olive-Demo-Exchange
4) Proposed sync: Thu May 21, 10:00am PT — 30m SecOps + Infra + Redwood performance runbook. Confirm if that works and I’ll send the invite.

Canary and performance plan (brief):
- Reserved canary: 3 x A100-equivalent, streaming-optimized runtime, KV caching enabled, batching disabled for streaming sessions.
- Test matrix: 3 payload profiles (median, 95th, large), concurrency sweep (1, 8, 30, 60), spike test 4x sustained for 10 minutes.
- Success criteria: median latency <= 250ms for median payload; p95 <= 600ms for median & p95 input; p99 objective TBD (we'll align on this in SecOps call).

I'll send calendar invite once you confirm Thu/10am PT and retention window. Attached: [redwood-latency-benchmarks-4k.pdf] — contains baseline numbers and a short explanation of progressive flushing for streaming.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
